profile.reading:
DartPoints operates its primary Baton Rouge, Louisiana data center at 7127 Florida Boulevard, designated BTR01, the larger and original of DartPoints' two Baton Rouge facilities. This facility traces its origin to Venyu, a company DartPoints describes as having operated for more than 30 years as Louisiana's premier data center infrastructure and cloud services provider, acquired by DartPoints on May 2, 2023 from its then-parent company, REV. REV's own published company history confirms it was formed through a 2019 merger of RTC, a Louisiana telephone cooperative founded in 1935 in Reserve, and EATEL, an Ascension Parish telecom provider that built one of the first fully fiber-to-the-home networks in the country and had itself acquired a company called Vision Communications in 2011, with the merged entity rebranding as REV in 2022. The facility spans 86,400 total square feet with a 25,800-square-foot data hall, drawing 2.5 megawatts of utility power against a 500-kilowatt critical IT load, cooled by 540 tons of N+1 redundant capacity, and connecting through 7 on-site network providers offering 1 to 100 gigabit connectivity. DartPoints markets the site's siting 50 feet above sea level and outside the 500-year floodplain as a resilience feature relevant to its Gulf Coast location, and states the facility has operated continuously for more than 15 years, consistent with an origin predating the DartPoints acquisition back into the Venyu and EATEL era, though no specific original opening year is disclosed. As is standard industry practice, tenant identities are not publicly disclosed, and no Uptime Institute Tier certification level is stated for this specific building (DartPoints' Shreveport facility, by contrast, is explicitly marketed as Tier III certified).

DartPoints markets itself company-wide as serving more than 900 enterprise customers, including universities, hospital systems, and Fortune 500 companies, across its roughly 11 data centers spanning 5 states.

reading.body:
DartPoints Baton Rouge 1 holds 2.5 MW of IT capacity, the second-largest published figure in Louisiana, where three facilities across four mapped sites report a combined 7.7 MW. At typical AI training density of 40 kW per rack, this 2.5 MW of IT load translates to roughly 60 racks. The facility sits at 7127 Florida Blvd on ground 50 feet above sea level, outside the 500-year floodplain.

The campus is one of three DartPoints facilities whose underlying real estate the operator owns outright following NOVA Infrastructure's majority acquisition of DartPoints in April 2025. DartPoints operates 11 facilities across ten markets in the Southeast and Midwest, serving more than 900 enterprise customers. The operator certifies SOC 2 Type II compliance and targets 99.999 percent uptime.

This campus contributes to a small but growing footprint in a state where published AI-ready capacity remains constrained. Louisiana's 7.7 MW of published capacity across mapped facilities places it far below data center hubs and reflects the regional market focus DartPoints pursues. Whether this site and others like it matter to AI scaling depends on whether regional operators can build power supply faster than the regional grid allows.
